description: Company Overview ACS (Allen Control Systems) is a defense technology company building precision robotic systems for the United States and its allies. Founded by two former U.S. Navy electrical engineers with deep experience in robotics and software, ACS brings together AI, computer vision, precision motion, and advanced hardware to solve complex defense challenges across land, air, and maritime environments. Our flagship product, Bullfrog, is an autonomous precision weapon system that transforms existing weapons into highly accurate counter-drone systems — giving warfighters a scalable, cost-effective response to one of the fastest-growing threats on the modern battlefield. Bullfrog is deployed with U.S. forces, and ACS works with organizations throughout the U.S. military and national security community. Following a $200 million Series B at a $2.2 billion valuation, ACS is rapidly expanding manufacturing, accelerating Bullfrog deployments, and developing the next generation of autonomous battlefield systems. This is an opportunity to join a proven, fast-moving team and help scale technology with direct, real-world impact on national security. ACS is headquartered in Austin, Texas, with additional operations in Alexandria, Virginia; Mountain View, California; and Huntsville, Alabama. For more information, visit allencontrolsystems.com . Our interns aren't fetching coffee or shadowing — they're working alongside the same engineers and product teams building the systems we ship. As a Technical Design Artist Intern , you'll work at the intersection of art, engineering, and real-time technology. You'll help build and improve the Unreal Engine 5 systems that bring our products to life — from 3D assets and materials to visual effects, tools, and content pipelines. This is early-career work with real stakes. You'll work closely with engineers and technical artists to solve problems, build things, and iterate on technology that needs to perform reliably in real-world environments. Location: Austin, TX (on-site) Duration: Summer 2027 (~10–12 weeks) Pay: Paid Internship (to be discussed during interviews) What You'll Do Build and integrate 3D assets, materials, textures, animations, and visual effects in Unreal Engine 5. Work closely with engineers and technical artists to develop and iterate on real-time visual systems. Create materials and shaders using Unreal Engine's Material Editor, including custom node-based and HLSL-based solutions where appropriate. Build tools and workflows that help artists and engineers work faster and more consistently. Use Blueprints and Python to automate repetitive tasks and improve content pipelines. Help investigate and solve performance issues across graphics, memory, rendering, and content. Work with Unreal Engine technologies such as Nanite, Lumen, Niagara, and Chaos. Collaborate with engineers and product teams to understand technical requirements and turn them into working visual solutions. Document tools, workflows, and technical decisions so others can build on your work. Take projects from an initial idea through implementation, feedback, and iteration. What We're Looking For Currently pursuing a degree in Computer Science, Game Development, Computer Graphics, Animation, Interactive Media, or a related field. Coursework, project, or internship experience with Unreal Engine, real-time graphics, technical art, 3D content creation, or game development. Experience working in Unreal Engine 5, including familiarity with the editor, Materials, and Blueprints. Experience with a 3D content creation tool such as Blender, Maya, or 3ds Max. Basic understanding of real-time rendering, including materials, lighting, textures, geometry, and performance. An interest in understanding how software and technical systems work. Strong problem-solving skills and attention to detail. Curiosity about working closely with engineers and learning how technical decisions affect the final product. A builder's mindset: you'd rather create something, get feedback, and iterate than wait for a perfect spec. A portfolio or examples of projects that demonstrate your work with Unreal Engine, 3D content, shaders, tools, visual effects, or other real-time technology. You'll Stand Out Experience with Python, C++, or HLSL. Experience building Unreal Engine tools or workflows with Blueprints or Python. Experience creating custom materials, shaders, or visual effects. Experience with Niagara, Nanite, Lumen, Control Rig, or Chaos. Experience with Houdini or procedural content generation. Experience using graphics or performance profiling tools such as RenderDoc, PIX, Unreal Insights, or the Unreal GPU Visualizer. Experience working directly with software engineers on a technical or creative project. Projects involving simulation, robotics, autonomy, embedded systems, or other real-time technology. Experience taking a project from prototype to a working, usable result. Why ACS Direct impact: Your work contributes to products that are built for real-world use — not stuck in a slide deck. Real ownership: You'll work directly with the engineers and product team building Bullfrog and contribute to real product decisions from day one. Small team, big scope: At a startup this size, interns take on meaningful problems and see their work move from concept to implementation. Cross-functional experience: Work alongside designers, product managers, and engineers to understand what it takes to build and ship a product. Mentorship: Learn from experienced engineers and product builders who have designed and fielded real defense systems.

description: Spacecraft represent the most pressing unmet need across the entire aerospace industry. As more launch vehicles come online and the cost to orbit decreases, more companies launching payloads to space continue to emerge. For the first time in history, this influx of payload companies combined with reduced launch costs has resulted in a massive increase in need for commercial spacecraft platforms, known as satellite buses. These buses hold the payloads of our customers and are flown on launch vehicles. Apex manufactures these satellite buses at scale using a combination of software, vertical integration, and hardware that is designed for manufacturing. Our spacecraft enable the future of society: ranging from earth observation to communications and more. We’d love for you to join us on our mission of providing humankind access to the galaxy beyond our planet. About the Role We are seeking talented engineering students to work closely with Apex’s Mission Integration team for an exciting internship opportunity. This role is ideal for someone who is passionate about space systems, eager to understand how spacecraft, launch vehicles, and ground systems come together, and motivated to learn how real missions are designed, integrated, and flown. As a Mission Integration Engineer Intern, you will support system-level mission planning and integration activities across active programs. You’ll gain exposure to end-to-end mission architecture, customer requirements, and cross-functional engineering collaboration. This role offers a unique opportunity to approach complex mission challenges from a systems perspective, with a focus on reliability, performance, and mission success. Internship Experience at Apex During the internship program at Apex, you’ll gain hands-on experience and meaningful professional growth. You’ll be assigned a mission-focused summer project that allows you to contribute directly to real spacecraft programs. Throughout the project, you’ll work closely with a dedicated mentor from the Mission Integration team while participating in technical learning sessions designed to deepen your understanding of satellite systems, launch environments, and mission operations. You’ll also connect with fellow interns and Apex engineers through community events and team activities, making this a well-rounded experience designed to launch your career in aerospace systems engineering. Mission Integration Engineering: Internship Focus Mission Integration Engineer Interns will assist with system-level mission integration activities across spacecraft programs. Responsibilities may include: Supporting mission architecture definition across spacecraft, launch vehicle, and operations elements Assisting with mission analysis tasks such as orbital mechanics, deployment concepts, and trajectory trade studies Helping generate and maintain mission-specific technical budgets (mass, power, data, pointing, etc.) Supporting requirements analysis, verification, and validation activities Assisting in the development of technical documentation, interface definitions, and integration procedures Collaborating with mechanical, electrical, software, and operations teams to ensure system compatibility Participating in internal design reviews, customer meetings, and technical discussions Learning how technical risks are identified, assessed, and mitigated at the system level This role emphasizes systems thinking, cross-disciplinary collaboration, and clear technical communication. Requirements Graduating in Fall 2027 or Spring 2028 Pursuing a BS or MS in Aerospace Engineering, Mechanical Engineering, Electrical Engineering, or a related field Strong interest in spacecraft systems, mission design, and space operations Coursework or project experience related to orbital mechanics, space systems, or systems engineering preferred Familiarity with tools such as Python, MATLAB, STK, GMAT, or similar analysis tools is a plus Strong organizational skills and attention to detail Ability to communicate technical concepts clearly and work effectively in a team environment U.S. Person status required due to access to export-controlled data Commitment This internship will begin in March 2027 or June 2027 and offers both full-time (40 hours/week) and part-time (minimum 20 hours/week) options. Full-time interns should be available to pause or adjust academic commitments (such as taking a semester off or enrolling part-time) for the duration of the 10–12 week program Part-time interns must maintain consistent availability during standard business hours to collaborate with their teams Compensation $45/hour #LI-RC1 Why Join Apex? Underneath it all is Atlas, our proprietary platform that keeps customers in control, secure by design, and never locked into one model. Why Now Brain Co. is entering its next phase of production deployments on a national scale with an elite team built from Palantir, Google, Meta, and Nvidia, and a growing footprint across government, insurance, health, and financial services. Joining now means shaping both the company and a new category of applied AI. Every project here ships to production and is expected to create measurable customer value and impact. You'll work alongside exceptional peers on some of the hardest problems in applied AI. It’s the kind of work you'll still be proud of in ten years from now. About the Role As an AI Product Intern , you will work closely with engineers, researchers, and product leaders to help design, build, and deploy AI-powered software solving real-world problems. This is a highly hands-on role where you’ll gain exposure to the full product lifecycle, from understanding customer needs to shipping production-grade AI applications. Help prototype and ship internal tools and customer-facing applications using modern web technologies Learn Product + Engineering in Practice: Work with product managers and engineers to translate customer problems into clear product requirements. Gain exposure to how AI models are integrated into real-world software systems Collaborate Closely: Partner with engineers, researchers, and operators to test, iterate, and improve AI-driven workflows. Participate in design discussions, sprint planning, and code reviews Optimize & Improve: Assist with improving performance, reliability, and usability of deployed applications. description: Company Overview Each year, 2.5 trillion hours are spent on household chores. At Matic, we’re on a mission to recapture that lost time, and we’re doing it by revolutionizing home robotics. Our first product, also called Matic, is a Wall-E-esque floor cleaning robot. We've built what amounts to "full self-driving in the home” with real-time 3D mapping, adaptive path-tracking, and a precise semantic understanding of the home. Our breakthroughs in spatial AI allow Matic to work reliably in real homes, using only RGB cameras and neural networks running on-device. Privacy First What happens in the home, stays in the home. Our robots are private by design, with all data processing performed by the robot itself, not in the cloud. Our Approach Before the iPhone, consumers adopted several distinct devices; cell phones, PDAs, and portable music players each served a particular need. We believe in a similar progression for home robotics, starting with single-purpose robots and building iteratively toward more complex capabilities over time. Our Culture Matic is a tight-knit and collaborative team, singularly focused on building products our customers will cherish. We're ultra-hardworking people committed to solving tough problems that save precious time and energy. About the role Help shape how people live with a robot in their home. At Matic, we’re bringing advanced robotics into everyday life, and design plays a central role in making that experience feel natural. We’re looking for a Product Design Intern with curiosity, a strong eye for craft, and a drive to turn ideas into something people can experience. You’ll work closely with design and engineering to explore new possibilities and make the product more intuitive, thoughtful, and delightful to use. Your time will be a mix of exploring concepts, building prototypes, sharing ideas, and refining interactions. You’ll use Figma and AI tools to bring concepts to life, test how they feel, and help the team decide what to build. With room to experiment, you’ll contribute to meaningful product work while developing your own design judgment. What You Will Do Explore and design experiences that connect people, software, and the physical world. Translate complex problems into clear flows, thoughtful interactions, and polished interfaces. Build interactive prototypes with Figma and AI tools to evaluate concepts and communicate design intent. Present your thinking, explore different directions, and refine your work through experimentation and team critique. Collaborate with engineers to understand possibilities, work through constraints, and bring ideas into the product. Follow designs through implementation, paying attention to the details that shape how an experience feels. Contribute to a consistent visual and interaction language across Matic’s product experience. What You Bring Curiosity about technology and a habit of asking how an experience could be better. Strong foundations in interaction and visual design, including layout, typography, hierarchy, and composition. A portfolio that shows thoughtful problem-solving, design craft, and your approach to developing ideas. School, personal, and internship projects are welcome. Comfort working in Figma and enthusiasm for exploring AI tools in your design process. The ability to communicate your ideas clearly and explain the decisions behind your work. Openness to feedback and a willingness to experiment, iterate, and learn. Care for the small details and an interest in how they contribute to the whole experience. Nice to Have Experience building functional prototypes with AI tools or code. Familiarity with motion design or spatial interactions. An understanding of mobile design patterns, accessibility, or design systems. Interest in consumer technology, robotics, and products that connect digital and physical experiences. Portfolio (Required) Show us how you think and what you make. We’d like to see the questions you explored, the approaches you tried, and the decisions that shaped your work. Interactive prototypes, experiments, and short demos are welcome alongside finished designs. If you used AI tools, tell us how they supported your process and where your design judgment guided the outcome. Please include your portfolio password, if applicable.

description: Who we are Melotech is revolutionizing media and entertainment. We create art through technology for humans to enjoy. In just 24 months, our work has been heard, watched and loved for over 4 billion minutes worldwide. Founded by entrepreneur and investor Soheil Mirpour, we are backed by top VCs Cherry Ventures, Speedinvest and GFC, alongside world-class angels from firms such as Spotify, Blackstone and KKR. What you will do Melotech is scaling fast, and organic reach is one of the engines behind it. As Growth Associate (Intern), you help run that engine end to end: the creators, the formats, the trends and the numbers behind them. This is an organic growth role first, measured on how much reach every hour and every euro brings back. You work directly with our founders, our Growth Manager, product and data team. Today that means a steady stream of new products that each deserve a shot at going viral across TikTok, Instagram Reels and YouTube Shorts. Your first job is to build the machine behind that: find the creators and communities that move culture, turn what works into repeatable playbooks, and run more experiments in a week than most teams run in a quarter. On a typical day, your tasks may include: Creator network: finding, briefing and paying creators and pages at scale, from small accounts with loyal audiences to the ones that set trends, and keeping the ones that deliver Seeding: getting our products into the formats and communities where they can travel, at the right moment and in the right volume Trend spotting: catching formats and memes early and moving on them within days, not weeks Experiments: running many cheap tests every week, with clear rules for what wins and what gets killed, and turning the winners into playbooks the team can repeat New channels: finding places where attention is still cheap, from fan pages and communities to platforms nobody on the team is using yet Organic and paid together: working with our Growth Manager so organic winners get scaled with paid, and what paid learns feeds back into organic Measurement: knowing which number answers which question, for example what saves and shares tell you that views do not, and what each view really costs Tooling: building the trackers, scripts and automations you need, with platform data and AI tools as your daily coworkers Who you are We're looking for a student or recent graduate who lives on the platforms and wants to learn how to make content travel. Typically, your profile will look like this: Platform fluency: you know TikTok, Instagram Reels and YouTube Shorts well and can explain why a post performs Hands-on experience: you have grown an account, a page or a side project, or supported a startup or brand on social Creator marketing: you enjoy working with creators and have a feel for content that looks native Creativity: you bring fresh ideas and test them in a structured way Analytical: you are comfortable with numbers and spreadsheets; SQL, Python or AI tools are a plus Pace: you thrive in a fast-paced and performance-oriented environment A big plus: you are a creator yourself, or have run pages with a real following Academics: pursuing or recently graduated with a degree at a top-tier university, with an outstanding academic record: grades, scholarships or awards to show for it What makes this exciting You own a lever the whole company feels. Every breakout you engineer shows up directly in how fast we can grow, at a fraction of what paid reach would cost. You're not a cog in the machine but the captain of your own ship, rewarded for performance and respected for leadership. Flat hierarchies mean that your voice matters, your ideas get implemented, and your impact is immediate. We pay competitive salaries and make you an owner of the business with equity. We work remotely to give you complete freedom over your life, while meeting regularly around the world for global offsites where we strategize, bond, and push boundaries together. What the process will look like We hire on a rolling basis. Earliest starting date is always ASAP. Once you begin our process, you can progress from start to offer within a week, depending on how quickly you can move through each stage: Initial interview: 30-minute introductory call, getting to know you Case interview: 90-minute case discussion, present and debate your skills Founder interview: 90-minute interview with our CEO, going deep on all topics Offer, contract signing and onboarding Note: As we are still in stealth, you will learn more about Melotech as you progress through the stages. By the end of the Founder interview, you will have a full grasp of our business and the details of your role.

description: At Upvest, we are on a mission to make investing as easy as spending money . Upvest empowers businesses to offer a wide range of investment products and the best experience in the field of capital market investment and retirement planning. Upvest’s Investment API is easy to integrate so that fintechs and financial institutions can save resources and fully focus on their core business. We are proud to partner with Europe’s leading Fintechs and financial institutions such as DKB, Revolut, N26 and Raisin. Founded in 2017 by Martin Kassing, Upvest now brings together over 270 talented professionals from more than 70 nationalities. Upvest is backed by €280M in total funding from world-class investors, including BlackRock, Tencent, Sapphire Ventures, and Bessemer Venture Partners, Earlybird, Notion Capital, and Motive . Our latest €105M funding round in March 2026 - led by Sapphire and Tencent - serves as a massive catalyst for our growth, allowing us to offer premier investment experience. About the role: As an AFC (Anti-Financial Crime) Operations Intern at Upvest, you’ll be at the forefront of our financial crime defense, playing a hands-on role in safeguarding our platform and our clients. You’ll execute Upvest’s first-line-of-defense (1st LoD) AFC processes day to day, the case work that keeps our brokerage infrastructure clean and compliant. This is a full-time, 6-month internship for someone with a first exposure to AFC / KYC or to the financial sector more broadly, for example through studies, customer support, banking operations, or a previous internship, who is ready to take on a real caseload and grow in autonomy. Depending on performance and business needs, the internship may be extended or converted into a full-time position. We’re looking for a reliable, detail-oriented person who understands the basics of KYC/AML and is comfortable managing high-volume operational tasks. What you’ll do: Conducting PEP and Sanctions screening, researching and dispositioning hits as true matches or false positives, with clear, well-documented rationale. Performing KYB checks for corporate onboarding. Carrying out KYC sample checks, transaction monitoring, and managing the resulting follow-ups with our clients. Executing and maintaining AFC procedures and controls in line with regulatory requirements and internal policy. Using and helping improve our automation and tooling to make case processing faster and more consistent, for example AI assistants, workflow automation (e.g. n8n), data validation and reporting in the Google Suite (Sheets, Apps Script) and Looker, and basic SQL for querying and cross-checking case data. Collaborating with the rest of the AFC Ops team and the AML team (2nd LoD) to continuously enhance our AML systems, tools and workflows. What you bring: A strong analytical mindset, exceptional attention to detail, and a genuine interest in compliance and financial-crime prevention. A foundational understanding of KYC/AML concepts, gained through your studies, a previous internship or early work experience in a fintech or financial institution. Early experience in a regulated environment is a plus, but not required. Comfort with high-volume, repeatable operational tasks and the discipline to keep quality consistent case after case. Curiosity about automation and the ability to quickly master new tools, systems and data. Excellent communication skills and a collaborative, reliable working style. A completed Bachelor’s degree is preferred but not essential. Good communication skills in English. How we Upvest in you: Impact-driven work: We’re building the infrastructure that will power the future of investing in Europe. It’s complex, ambitious, and meaningful. You’ll work with modern technologies and create something entirely new. No legacy systems, no limits. Team celebrations: Participate in company-wide events, such as UpFest, dinners, offsites and our Holiday party, to connect with colleagues and celebrate our achievements. Inclusion : We’re committed to a culture where everyone belongs and thrives. Our Employee Resources Groups foster inclusion and connection, like Upfem Black at Upvest, Up&Out, and UpVergent. Our Values: Make it easy for others. We simplify the complex and act with the best intentions Own the outcome. We are proactive, fast and confident to get the job done, valuing progress over perfection. Rise to the challenge. We aim high and push the boundaries. We stay curious, learn and celebrate our wins together. Tell the story. We start with the Why to align on purpose. We are transparent and share knowledge to empower and inspire others. Compensation is a set amount for the Intern role with no range.

Remote-first with flexibility built in

description:
Activation, The Operators and Negotiators | Discovery, The Intent Capturers

We are a 1,000-piece puzzle. Each of us is essential, interconnected, and intentionally designed. Together we create something powerful: media that matters, growth that lasts, and a culture we are proud to build.

As part of our Activation and Discovery teams, you'll help brands connect with audiences through paid social advertising and strengthen their visibility across search engines, AI-powered platforms, and emerging discovery experiences.

Our Activation team, The Operators and Negotiators, brings media strategies to life through precise execution and optimization. Our Discovery team, The Intent Capturers, helps brands show up where people search, explore, and make decisions. Together, these disciplines connect audience insight, content, and technology to drive measurable growth.

ABOUT THE CO-OP PROGRAM

Our six-month, full-time Co-op Program gives students and emerging talent the opportunity to contribute to real client work while building foundational skills in digital media.

As a paid member of Attention Arc, you'll work 40 hours per week alongside experienced professionals, gaining exposure to paid social advertising, Search Engine Optimization (SEO), Generative Engine Optimization (GEO), and the evolving world of digital discoverability.

Throughout the program, you'll:

  • Build your skills: Develop platform knowledge through training, mentorship, and practical assignments.

  • Contribute to client work: Support campaigns, research initiatives, and performance analysis.

  • Explore what's next: Investigate how AI and emerging technologies are changing media and brand discovery.

  • Take ownership: Manage increasingly complex assignments as your capabilities develop.

  • Connect across teams: Understand how different disciplines work together to deliver client results.

You don't need to arrive as an expert. Bring curiosity, initiative, and a willingness to contribute.

WHAT YOU'LL DO

You'll support paid social campaigns and discoverability projects, helping teams turn research and performance data into meaningful action.

Key Responsibilities

Paid Social

  • Assist with campaign setup, monitoring, and optimization across Meta, TikTok, LinkedIn, Pinterest, Reddit, and emerging platforms.

  • Learn campaign fundamentals, including audience targeting, creative placements, bidding, budgets, and performance objectives.

  • Monitor campaign pacing and key performance indicators to assess progress against client goals.

  • Analyze performance data to identify trends and potential optimization opportunities.

  • Support audience and creative research to understand what resonates with different consumer segments.

  • Maintain campaign documentation, reporting, and quality assurance standards.

  • Complete relevant platform training and certifications.

SEO, GEO & Discoverability

  • Develop foundational knowledge of SEO, Generative Engine Optimization (GEO), and Answer Engine Optimization (AEO).

  • Conduct keyword, topic, and audience intent research to understand how people find information and discover brands.

  • Research brand visibility across Google, ChatGPT, Gemini, Perplexity, and emerging AI search experiences.

  • Assist with evaluating website content, metadata, internal linking, and other foundational SEO elements.

  • Support competitive research and content audits to identify opportunities to improve visibility, relevance, and authority.

  • Organize and analyze data using Google Search Console, Google Analytics 4, Semrush, Ahrefs, or similar tools.

  • Participate in projects exploring how AI-powered search influences consumer behavior and brand discovery.

  • Document findings and contribute to recommendations with guidance from experienced team members.

Collaboration & Professional Development

  • Partner with teams across Activation, Discovery, Planning, Analytics, Strategy, and Technology.

  • Prepare reports, presentations, and research summaries that communicate findings clearly.

  • Participate in team meetings, learning sessions, and relevant client or partner discussions.

  • Apply AI-enabled tools responsibly to support research, analysis, and workflow efficiency.

  • Share observations on platform developments, industry trends, and new technologies.

WHAT YOU'LL BRING

Experience & Technical Expertise

  • Currently pursuing or recently completed a degree in Marketing, Advertising, Communications, Business, Analytics, Computer Science, or a related field. All majors are welcome with a demonstrated interest in digital media or technology.

  • Interest in paid social advertising, SEO, AI-powered search, and digital marketing.

  • Foundational proficiency in Microsoft Excel or Google Sheets, including data organization and basic analysis.

About Labs

DoorDash Labs is an independent team within DoorDash. We're hiring software engineer interns to work at the intersection of software engineering and robotics to solve key business problems with elegant technical solutions. If you have a passion for applying robotics solutions to a service loved by millions of people, then we want to talk to you! 

About the Teams

We are hiring Software Engineer interns across our Perception, Autonomy Platform, and DoorDash Air Cloud (Foundry) team. Please review the team descriptions below to learn about each. Selected candidates will be notified of which team is interested in pursuing their candidacy. 

  Perception: The Perception team helps Dot understand the world through vision foundation models and VLMs, supported by lidar and radar for safety. We tackle rare scenarios, adverse weather, and advances in reinforcement learning and end-to-end driving to make deliveries faster and smoother. We're seeking exceptional engineers in machine learning, computer vision, and state estimation to turn cutting-edge research into profitable autonomous delivery.

Autonomy Platform: The Autonomy Platform team is responsible for the software foundation that Dot runs on. We build a wide variety of software frameworks for ensuring the robot operates reliably at an ever-increasing scale. This includes everything from designing the robot's operating system, building petabyte-scale data processing pipelines in the cloud, and optimizing nanosecond-level compute of bleeding-edge AI models. We are systems-oriented thinkers and hands-on builders who are excited to advance the state of the art in autonomy.

Doordash Air Cloud (Foundry): The Air Cloud team, also known as Foundry, builds the cloud software that powers autonomous delivery across DoorDash—from the moment an order is placed and deemed eligible for drone or robot delivery, through merchant handoff, to flight management. 

About the Role

We believe interns are essential to our mission of attracting and retaining top talent. During our 12-week Software Engineer internship, interns are completely immersed in their teams and will have the opportunity to develop, maintain, and ship products. As an intern, you will directly impact our business by collaborating with your team to solve real problems for our customers.


Applicants must be authorized to work in the U.S. to be considered for this position. F-1 students are eligible if they are using Curricular Practical Training (CPT). DoorDash does not support students on J-1 visas for internships at this time.

The 2027 internship program will be hosted in person at a Doordash Labs office in either San Francisco or Sunnyvale Labs. You will have an opportunity to select your preferred location(s) and team preferences during the application process.

Eulerity is an AI marketing automation platform that makes digital advertising simple for businesses of all sizes, from local franchises to global enterprises. The Rendering & Animation team (R&A) builds the graphics engine which renders the canvas for all Figma applications. Our mission is to make rendering performant, feature-rich, reliable, maintainable and extendible across all products & surfaces. The team plays a core, bedrock role for the company because it underpins the technology driving the user experience, touching many other teams, and as such is one of the most impactful areas of Figma.

The R&A team is devoted to hiring individuals with graphics expertise. We are interested in a variety of sub-domains, including 2D GPU-driven rendering, computational geometry & vector graphics, animation frameworks, anti-aliasing algorithms, shader effects, and more recently branching into video/image processing. A PhD Intern specializing in any of these areas would be a phenomenal fit for the team with a lot of exciting projects available.

As an intern on our team, you'll take ownership of a high-impact project at the intersection of your technical strengths and our most pressing graphics, rendering, or media challenges. You'll work closely with your intern manager, team leads, and collaborators across 1–2 partner teams to deliver tangible results within your internship. This is an opportunity to do significant, portfolio-worthy work that directly supplies Figma's visual platform.

This is a 12 or 16-week internship role that can be held from one of our US hubs (San Francisco or New York) starting in May or June of 2027.

What you'll do at Figma:

  • Learn from industry graphics engineers and participate as an embedded team member of the Rendering & Animation team
  • Collaborate with engineers, PMs, designers, and researchers to scope and execute your work
  • Develop, validate, and document solutions from prototypes to production-ready systems
  • Drive projects that apply research insights to meaningful product challenges
  • Contribute to exciting domain areas; some examples: crafting and optimizing shaders for sophisticated effects, investigating improvements to anti-aliasing algorithms, improving media processing capabilities, animating spline interpolation, and more!

We'd love to hear from you if you have:

  • Current enrollment as a 4th or 5th year senior PhD student pursuing a PhD in Computer Graphics, Media Processing, or a related field
  • Experience working with OpenGL, WebGL, WebGPU, Vulkan or Metal and their respective shader languages (GLSL, WGSL) or other low-level graphics APIs
  • Proficiency in either C++ or Rust
  • A track record of rigorous problem-solving through academic or applied research, with experience thinking holistically about use cases and the low-level technology required

While it's not required, it's an added plus if you also have:

  • Demonstrated expertise in computer graphics, supported by publications at conferences such as SIGGRAPH, Eurographics, High Performance Graphics, NVIDIA GTC, or Pacific Graphics
  • Proficiency in WebAssembly, web graphics, 2D graphics, performance optimization, animation, geometry, or media
  • Interest in art and design applications
  • Experience using AI tools (e.g., GitHub Copilot, ChatGPT, Claude) to write, debug, and optimize code
  • Related industry experience via a past internship or full-time role
  • Strong communication and interpersonal skills, with demonstrated experience collaborating across functions

At Figma, one of our values is Grow as you go. We believe in hiring smart, curious people who are excited to learn and develop their skills. If you’re excited about this role but your past experience doesn’t align perfectly with the points outlined in the job description, we encourage you to apply anyways. You may be just the right candidate for this or other roles.

description:
About the company 

General Matter enriches uranium.

We are designing, building, and operating the world’s lowest-cost enrichment services, here in the US.  

In the process, we are restoring America’s ability to produce nuclear fuel to power AI, advanced manufacturing and critical industries our country relies on to remain competitive. 

Fuel drives the cost of advanced reactor electricity production, and enrichment drives the cost of the fuel that advanced reactors consume.  Reliable, low-cost enrichment is the catalyst for the nuclear Renaissance now under way.

Our mission is to make nuclear not only the cleanest and safest source of baseload power, but also the most affordable.  We believe abundant nuclear energy will lead to a post-scarcity society. 

We were incubated inside Founders Fund, like Anduril and Palantir before us, and are backed by over a dozen of the world's top venture capital firms.  

Our lean, world-class team of engineers and operators is applying a first-principles approach to solving the problem of nuclear fuel production.  

We are a mission-driven company with a culture of urgency, accountability, and transparency. 

Help us build a high-energy society by making the cleanest, safest form of baseload energy the most affordable. 

About This Role

General Matter builds its own technology: the software, firmware, control systems, and infrastructure that run an industrial nuclear fuel facility. At most companies, a security bug costs you data. Here, the software we build, and any security vulnerabilities we miss, touch the real world. The Security team's job is to find those gaps before anyone else does. We do that through offensive testing, code audits, design reviews, and hardening the systems we ship. 

As an intern on the team, you'll attack General Matter's products and infrastructure, while working with the engineers who own them to fix what you find. Targets include web apps, APIs, Linux and Windows hosts, cloud environments, embedded devices, and industrial controllers. You'll own real projects from start to finish, and you won't be writing policy documents

Responsibilities

  • Break everything you touch, then help us fix it. 
  • Run penetration tests against General Matter networks, services, web applications, and APIs. Prove what you find with working proof-of-concept exploits. 
  • Audit source code and features for security vulnerabilities in languages like Python, C, C++, Rust, Go, and TypeScript. Then build static analysis rules or CI checks so the same class of bug can't come back. 
  • Reverse engineer and attack embedded devices and industrial equipment on an isolated test bench. That includes firmware extraction, binary analysis on x86 and ARM, debug interfaces (JTAG, SWD, UART), and PLC and industrial protocol implementations (Modbus, EtherNet/IP, OPC UA). 
  • Do threat modeling and adversarial design reviews with software, controls, and hardware engineers. Help design a secure architecture for systems before they ship. 
  • Assess third-party software, devices, and services before they get into our environment, and work with vendors and suppliers to get the issues fixed. 
  • Attack cloud and identity infrastructure, including IAM misconfigurations, exposed secrets, privilege escalation paths, and CI/CD supply chain weaknesses. 
  • Build automated tooling that spots known security exposures and keeps running after your internship ends. 
  • Present your findings and fixes to the engineers and leaders who own the systems. 

Basic Qualifications

  • Currently pursuing a Bachelor's, Master's, or PhD in Computer Science, Computer Engineering, Electrical Engineering, Cybersecurity, or a related field 
  • Security experience in one or more of the following: C, C++, Rust, Go, Python, x86, ARM, cryptography, reverse engineering, embedded systems, or network protocols. 
  • A strong understanding of common vulnerability classes and how to exploit them, such as SQLi, XSS, CSRF, SSRF, memory corruption, and authentication or authorization flaws. 
  • Experience auditing code and features, and comfort reading large codebases you didn't write. 
  • Strong investigative and analytical problem-solving skills. You keep digging after the obvious attacks fail.

Advanced Reentry Technologies

Who We Are:

Inversion is an aerospace and defense company pioneering advanced reentry technology to enable next-generation capabilities from space. By combining high-performance materials, precision aerodynamics, and mission-driven autonomy, Inversion is transforming reentry into an operational capability for an entirely new class of missions.

The company’s highly maneuverable reentry spacecraft, Arc, is designed for rapid global cargo delivery, hypersonic testing, and other national security missions that require precise, controlled flight through the atmosphere. Arc creates an entirely new transportation domain, unlocking unprecedented speed and global reach.

Headquartered in Los Angeles, Inversion designs, manufactures, and integrates its spacecraft under one roof, enabling the company to move rapidly from concept to flight. The company is backed by leading investors including Y Combinator, Spark Capital, and Lockheed Martin Ventures, with customers across the U.S. government and commercial space industry.

Position Overview:

As an RF Engineering Intern, you will support the verification, validation, integration, and performance characterization of flight and ground RF/Telemetry systems for Inversion’s next-generation re-entry vehicles. You will sit within the Avionics team and work closely with engineers on hands-on RF testing, antenna and GPS integration, communications system validation, and ground station compatibility efforts, helping take systems from benchtop validation through integrated hardware testing and mission-readiness verification.

You will be a member of the Avionics team, supporting the development, test, integration, and troubleshooting of critical communications hardware and systems for cutting-edge maneuverable reentry vehicles. This is a practical, lab-heavy internship for students interested in spacecraft communications, telemetry, antennas, and RF system integration in a fast-paced aerospace environment.

Key Responsibilities:

  • Work closely with RF engineers and cross-functional teammates to build practical understanding of how aerospace RF and telemetry systems are developed, tested, integrated, and prepared for flight applications.
  • Perform component-, subsystem-, and system-level RF test and measurement activities using standard laboratory equipment such as spectrum analyzers, network analyzers, signal generators, oscilloscopes, and power meters.
  • Support over-the-air and antenna test activities, including range setup and validation, as needed.
  • Support GPS testing and integration for the Arc vehicle.
  • Support ground station compatibility testing, including potential travel to test sites.
  • Help test and evaluate in-house RF hardware, including SDR-based systems.
  • Collect, process, and document RF test data and support generation of test reports and summaries.
  • Assist with test automation and analysis tools using Python, MATLAB, or similar tools.

Required Qualifications:

  • Must be enrolled in a bachelor’s, master's or doctorate degree program in an engineering, physics or math discipline.
  • GPA of 3.0 or above.
  • 3+ months of applied engineering experience (internship, laboratory, and personal/team project experience is applicable).
  • Coursework or project experience in RF, antennas, electromagnetics, or communications systems.
  • Strong problem-solving, written and verbal communication skills, with the ability to present technical results clearly to multidisciplinary teams.

Desired Qualifications:

  • Hands-on familiarity with RF lab equipment such as a spectrum analyzer or VNA.
  • Experience with Altium, HFSS, or similar RF/PCB design tools.
  • Completed an RF or antenna course.
  • Experience designing a circuit board.
  • Experience designing a simple microwave antenna or filter.
  • Hands-on experience through Formula SAE, student rocketry, CubeSat, robotics, or similar engineering projects.
  • Previous internship experience at a space, aerospace, or hardware startup.
  • Experience with Python or MATLAB for test automation or data analysis.
  • Experience with antenna test methods.
  • Familiarity with S-band and L-band communication or telemetry systems.
  • Familiarity with S-parameters and their use in evaluating RF component and system performance.

Our office headquarters is located in Playa Vista, CA. This position requires in-office presence.

The California annual base hourly rate for this role is currently $38-$41.  Pay Grades are determined by role, level, location, and alignment with market data.  Individual pay will be determined on a case-by-case basis and may vary based on the following considerations: interviews and an assessment of several factors that are unique to each candidate, job-related skills, relevant education and experience, certifications, abilities of the candidate and internal equity.

About Neuralink:

We are creating devices that enable a bi-directional interface with the brain. These devices allow us to restore movement to the paralyzed, restore sight to the blind, and revolutionize how humans interact with their digital world.

Team Description:

The Pathology Team plays a critical role in the evaluation of both macroscopic and microscopic tissue samples derived from our preclinical studies. The team encompasses specialized units focused on  Anatomic Pathology, Histology, Digital Pathology, and Laboratory Operations.

Job Description and Responsibilities:

As a Histopathology Intern, you will support both routine histology workflows and the development of next-generation tissue preparation and imaging techniques. In this role, you will work closely with pathologists and histology specialists to evaluate tissue-device interactions, with a primary focus on benchmarking, optimizing, and scaling novel volumetric histology pipelines such as tissue clearing and lightsheet microscopy. You will apply foundational biological and laboratory principles in a fast-paced environment and are expected to:
  • Assist in the optimization and validation of next-generation histology workflows, specifically focusing on aqueous and solvent-based tissue clearing methods and lightsheet fluorescence microscopy (LSFM) for 3D tissue visualization
  • Help maintain, calibrate, and operate advanced optical hardware, lightsheet imaging systems, and automated histology equipment
  • Support routine tissue processing, embedding, sectioning (microtomy), slide preparation, and standard/special staining protocols
  • Document experimental protocols, image acquisition parameters, and data analysis pipelines in compliance with Good Documentation Practices (GDP) and laboratory SOPs
  • Work cross-functionally with Pathology, Preclinical, and Surgical Engineering teams to prepare tissue samples, acquire high-resolution datasets, and support study deliverables
  • Assist with laboratory upkeep, including reagent preparation, chemical and biohazardous waste disposal, and inventory management

Required Qualifications: 

  • Currently pursuing a Bachelor’s or Master’s degree in Biomedical Engineering, Neuroscience, Biology, Chemistry, Materials Science, or a related discipline
  • Basic understanding of anatomy, neuroanatomy, and light/fluorescence microscopy principles
  • Familiarity with laboratory safety standards, fume hood operation, and handling biohazardous/chemical materials
  • Strong written and verbal communication skills with high attention to detail

Preferred Qualifications: 

  • 6+ months of relevant academic coursework or wet-lab experience handling biological tissues and standard histology techniques (e.g., tissue fixation, sectioning, or fluorescence imaging)
  • Direct hands-on experience or coursework in tissue clearing protocols and lightsheet fluorescence microscopy
  • Experience with 3D image analysis software or large volume rendering tools (e.g., Imaris, ImageJ/Fiji, or Python/MATLAB image processing libraries)
  • Exposure to medical device research and/or  neuroscience applications
  • Proven ability to learn new laboratory equipment quickly and troubleshoot technical procedures

Additional Requirements and Competencies:

  • Ability to work flexible hours, including off-hours and weekends
  • Comfortable working in a controlled laboratory environment with potential exposure to extreme temperatures, fumes, and biohazardous materials or chemicals, including formalin.
  • Ability to lift and maneuver up to 45 pounds to manage large volumes of chemical waste, reposition large animals, and perform other physically demanding tasks as required.

description:
Engineering Co-op

About Us

Salient Motion is building a modular motion and actuation platform that is redefining how aerospace, defense, and industrial systems are designed, built, and deployed. We move fast, operate with high ownership, and expect real contribution from every member of the team. Co-ops are treated like engineers, not observers. You will own real work, ship to production hardware, and leave with a body of work you can point to.

Role Overview

As an Engineering Co-op, you will embed with our engineering team across mechanical, electrical, software, manufacturing, and systems-level work for six months or longer. Unlike a short summer internship, this role is designed for students who want to take a project from specification through qualification, see a full product cycle, and operate as a contributing member of the team.

This is a hands-on role in a fast-paced startup environment. You will be expected to ramp quickly, take ownership of a defined workstream, and ship work that goes into customer programs.

What You Will Do

  • Own a scoped engineering workstream from design through test and release, with support from a senior engineer
  • Design, build, and test electro-mechanical systems and subassemblies on active customer programs
  • Build, maintain and improve test fixtures, data collection infrastructures
  • Firmware bring-up, design validation tests for electronics boards
  • Lead prototyping, assembly, and hands-on lab and shop work
  • Plan and execute engineering tests, collect data, and present results to the team
  • Drive manufacturing and supplier activities including part preparation, first-article inspection, and validation
  • Build and improve engineering and documentation processes that outlast your co-op term
  • Partner with senior engineers and program leaders, and present progress in design and program reviews

What We Are Looking For

  • Enrolled in a Bachelor's or Master's program in Mechanical Engineering, Electrical Engineering, Mechatronics, or a related field, with the ability to commit to a minimum 6-month co-op rotation
  • Available for a full-time term, whether a full academic semester, summer plus a connecting semester, or two consecutive semesters
  • Strong curiosity and willingness to work across disciplines
  • Comfortable in a lab or shop environment with hardware and tools
  • Clear communicator who can document work, present results, and ask thoughtful questions
  • Prior hands-on experience through projects, labs, clubs, personal builds, or a previous internship or co-op is a strong plus

What You Will Gain

  • Ownership of real production-bound hardware over a long enough window to see it ship
  • Exposure to aerospace and defense engineering standards and practices through a full program cycle
  • Mentorship from experienced engineers and direct access to founders and program leadership
  • A portfolio of shipped work and a reference from a startup that moved on your contributions
  • Co-ops completing 9+ months in good standing are evaluated for a full-time return offer at graduation

Co-op Details

  • Full-time, paid co-op, with pay tiered by commitment length:
    • 6-month rotation: $28 to $34/hr
    • 9 to 12 month rotation: $34 to $40/hr
  • Minimum 6-month commitment; 9 to 12 month rotations preferred
  • Start dates flexible to align with your school's co-op calendar. Common cadences include January to June, July to December, and July to June for full-year rotations
  • Onsite in Hawthorne, CA; relocation support includes a $1,200/month housing stipend for students relocating more than 50 miles

About the role:

As a Technical Writing Intern, you will test and document new product features that help our global user base analyze and gather insights from their data. During your internship, you’ll partner directly with your tech writer mentor, as well as collaborate with other teams across the business to deliver a significant new documentation project that benefits our customers. You will collaborate across the company to determine the best solution for your technical challenge. Interns will take their project from ideation through implementation, iterating and gathering feedback along the way. Potential projects include developing new tutorials and examples, creating video and gif content to illustrate key concepts, or implementing information architecture transformations to optimize content for AI agents. 

During your internship you will:

  • Write clear and accurate documentation that enables Sigma customers to use the product to effectively and efficiently achieve their goals. 
  • Deploy documentation and gather insights from customer metrics to aid you in making better decisions and improve your business acumen and collaboration skills.
  • Work closely with the development team (including engineers, designers, and product managers) throughout the development process to understand features and functionality at the level of a subject matter expert.
  • Participate in cross-functional planning, bug bashes, and strategic discussions. 
  • Explore and validate product features through rigorous testing, sharing insights with the team.
  • Translate complex technical details into clear, digestible documentation and release notes.
  • Work collaboratively and closely with other writers to ensure consistent and cohesive content, style, and messaging.
  • Draft, review, and publish content in a docs-as-code workflow with AI tooling in the loop.
  • Improve existing documentation based on feedback from customer-facing teams and actively address knowledge gaps, prioritizing user empowerment for all audiences.
  • Develop visually captivating, dynamic documentation that includes diagrams, screenshots, and other visual aids.

What we’re looking for:

A cover letter is required for applications to be considered. Please share why you’re interested in Sigma and how you meet the criteria listed in this "What we're looking for" section.

  • Applicants must be pursuing at least a Bachelor’s or a Master’s degree in Computer Science or a related field
  • Exceptional written and spoken communication skills, emphasizing clarity and approachability for various audiences.
  • A genuine desire to learn new things daily and to translate complex topics into actionable user assistance for end users. 
  • Solid project management and communication abilities. You love to find the right resources and can own tasks end to end with minimal supervision.
  • Ability to collaborate and work in a team environment.
  • Able to commit 40 hrs a week for 12 weeks in-person in our San Francisco, CA or New York, NY office 

Additional job details

Interns at Sigma are compensated with an hourly rate and relocation bonus (where applicable). Our hourly rate for this role ranges from $36.00 - $42.00 per hour.

Note: We have an in-office work environment in both our SF & NYC office.

At SK Hynix Memory Solution, we're at the forefront of semiconductor innovation, developing advanced memory solutions that power everything from smartphones to data centers. As a global leader in DRAM and NAND flash technologies, we drive the evolution of advancing mobile technology, empowering cloud computing, and pioneering future technologies. Our cutting-edge memory technologies are essential in today's most advanced electronic devices and IT infrastructure, enabling enhanced performance and user experiences across the digital landscape.

We're looking for innovative minds to join our mission of shaping the future of technology. At SK Hynix Memory, you'll be part of a team that's pioneering breakthrough memory solutions while maintaining a strong commitment to sustainability. We're not just adapting to technological change – we're driving it, with significant investments in artificial intelligence, machine learning, and eco-friendly solutions and operational practices. As we continue to expand our market presence and push the boundaries of what's possible in semiconductor technology, we invite you to be part of our journey to creating the next generation of memory solutions that will define the future of computing.

 

Internship Duration: 6 months

Hours: 40 hours per week

Start Date: November 2026 or December 2026 

 

About the Role:

The candidate will be responsible for supporting device level testing and validation of Enterprise NVMe SSDs and its features. This includes developing white/black box test cases for the validation NVMe SSD features, creating test scripts for verifying features defined by the NVMe and Open Compute Project (OCP) specification, and also test Vendor Unique features. The candidate will also be responsible for upkeep and maintenance of assigned lab equipment which includes Enterprise servers and PC systems. Understanding of AI tools, including development of Agentic Agents is highly desired.

 

Responsibilities:

  • Utilizing AI tools and concepts, develop test cases for features defined by the Product’s PRD, NVMe and OCP specifications.
  • Develop test cases for features defined by Customer or Vendor Unique specifications
  • Create automated scripts and run above developed tests cases against NVMe SSDs to validate and or verify their compliance to standard.
  • Prepare tests systems which includes OS installations (Linux/Windows/VMWare), Network connection, and also NVMe SSD firmware updating for testing.
  • Utilizing AI resources, develop Agentic Agents for daily operations, including test scripts development, internal qualification, and integration to Test Management System.
  • Responsible to upkeep and maintenance of assigned lab equipment such as Enterprise servers and Computer PCs.

 

Minimum Qualifications:

  • Currently pursuing or a recent graduate of a Bachelor’s degree in Science, Mathematics, or a related field.
  • Proficient in working with computer systems which includes platforms running Linux and Windows.
  • Coding or scripting experience preferred (Java, Python).
  • Understanding of AI tools and workflow integration using Agentic Agents.
  • Candidate must possess strong analytical and problem-solving skills to help in finding root cause and resolution of problems
  • Candidate must possess enthusiasm and willingness to learn on their own, as they must be able to work independently without much supervision

 

Preferred Qualifications:

  • Understanding of Storage and NVMe SSDs and NVMe controllers.
  • Experience with various Operating Systems, VMWare ESXi and other Hypervisors

Overview: A chip isn't a product until it's a working system. These teams cover both ends of that: getting silicon to boot and validate correctly,building the board, power, mechanical, thermal, packaging and IO around it. You submit one application, you have one recruiter screen - then we match you to the specific team below and location that fits best.

  • Systems & Silicon Validation: Post-silicon testing of physical chips and integrated systems to ensure they meet all functional, electrical, and performance specs.
  • System Software: Development of foundational software, including firmware, drivers, and operating systems, that directly controls and interfaces with hardware.
  • System Design: The process of defining, integrating, and mapping out hardware components such as PCBs, software modules, and interfaces into a complete product blueprint.
  • System Architecture: Define the high-level structural framework, interfaces, and data-flow pathways between the CPU, memory, and peripherals.
  • Packaging: A package is what is placed between the silicon and the board; and its design requires detailed electrical, electromagnetic, and mechanical simulations and analysis. 

This role is on-site based out of Toronto, Ontario or Vancouver, British Columbia.

 

Who You Are

  • Currently pursuing a BS, MS, or PhD in EE, Computer Engineering, Computer Science or Mechanical Engineering
  • Coursework or projects in embedded systems, microwave and signal integrity, board-level design, or thermal/mechanical engineering using low-level programming (C/C++, Python) or hardware design and/or simulation tools (e.g., CAD, FEA, Verilog).
  • Problem solver with strong foundational knowledge in one of these areas: electrical engineering, digital logic, computer architecture, or thermal/mechanical.
  • Curious learner who is passionate about the intersection of software, silicon architecture, and the physical constraints of chip packaging and printed circuit boards (PCBs).

What We Need

  • Systems & Silicon Validation: Assist in post-silicon testing of physical microchips under real-world workloads to ensure they meet all functional, electrical, and performance specifications.
  • System Software: Contribute to developing foundational software—including firmware, drivers, and operating systems—that directly controls and interfaces with the semiconductor hardware.
  • System Design & Architecture: Help map out, define, and evaluate high-level structural frameworks, optimizing the power delivery and high-speed performance benchmarks of both the silicon components and the underlying PCBs.
  • Semiconductor Packaging & Mechanical Design: Design and layout, Electromagnetic (signal integrity and power integrity), mechanical design, and stress analysis

What You Will Learn

  • Hands-on silicon experience using industry-standard lab equipment to bridge the gap between theoretical hardware design, physical packaging layouts, and real-world chips.
  • Low-level software development by writing production-grade firmware, device drivers, and diagnostic tools that run directly on bare metal.
  • Mechanical & thermal engineering for electronics by learning how structural stress, heat dissipation, thermal expansion, and mechanical shock affect the structural integrity and performance of PCBs and packages.
  • Cross-functional collaboration working alongside world-class architects, mechanical designers, package engineers, and software teams to understand how complex, large-scale chip ecosystems are built from scratch.

About the Role

The Speculative Decoding team at Together AI builds the draft models and algorithms that let large language models generate faster without changing their outputs. Our speculators run in production on frontier open models such as DeepSeek, Kimi and GLM. Our work sits at the intersection of model training, inference algorithms and serving systems, and we co-design all three to lower the cost and latency of generation.

As a research intern, you will dive into open questions in speculative decoding: new drafter architectures and verification schemes, knowledge distillation and training recipes that align draft and target models, and drafters that adapt as traffic shifts. You will train and fine-tune draft models at scale on dedicated GPU clusters, and test your ideas against realistic serving workloads, including long-context and agentic traffic.

Projects aim to answer important research questions in speculative decoding, enabling faster generation on frontier models, drafters that keep pace with changing workloads, and robust, reproducible evaluation under real traffic.

  • Speculative Speculative Decoding (ICLR 2026)

  • Beat the Long Tail: Distribution-Aware Speculative Decoding for RL Training (MLSys 2026)

  • Research and prototype new efficient speculative decoding algorithms and draft model architectures
  • Train, fine-tune and distill draft models, and design rigorous experiments to validate hypotheses.
  • Implement optimized version for serving engines to show efficacy in real world workloads
  • Communicate the plans, progress, and results of projects to the broader team
